text: Morgan Fairfax is an evil scientist working for the D.O.E. (Department of Environment), he tries to flood the West Coast in PKNA #4 "Terremoto" ("Earthquake") but was stopped by the Duck Avenger and Uno. He would later on ally himself with Oberon De Spair and work for Belgravia. In issue 45, Fairfax is shown to have become overweight. In Might and Power, Fairfax meets Lieutenant McCoy in jail. McCoy reveals his actual identity as the Evronian Grrodon, and Fairfax puts his projects to his service in order to get back at the world that never understood him.

Mr. Griff is a character from Hercules. He is an elderly Griffin who lives at the Elysian Sunset Rest Home in Room XXIII (23). His one appearance was the episode "Hercules and the Griffin". Mr. Griff was tasked ages ago with guarding the first diamond crafted by Hephaestus. Griff's greatest foe was King Arismap, the leader of the band of thieving mountain gnomes known as the Arismapse. Always did King Arismap and his cronies attempt to make off with the gemstone, but Griff always managed to foil them. Of course, Arismap was not one to give up so easily. Because of this, Griff refused to ever leave his nest, which is why it was brought along with him when he entered his winter years.
Morgana is an evil sorceress who appears in the Disney Jr. animated series Sofia the First.
The is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

Mr. Stenchy, also known as Experiment 254, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to use his alluring charm to get the enemy to take him back to their headquarters, where, 48 hours after his activation, he emits a foul odor that makes the location inhospitable. His one true place is on Plorgonar (Pleakley's home planet), where, unlike most places in the galaxy, his stench is considered a rare and valuable perfume.

Mrs. Sickly, also known as Experiment 255, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. She is designed to make people sick with her nauseatingly sweet fumes. She appears in the Stitch! anime.

Mrs. Bluveridge is a minor character in Muppet Treasure Island. She is the owner of the Benbow Inn and a motherly figure of sorts to Jim Hawkins, Gonzo, and Rizzo the Rat. She never intends to offend any of her guests with the way she talks (such as when using the word "pigsty"). Mrs. Bluveridge has a great deal of hearing, as she responds to what others are saying no matter where they are (eg, "To the northwest: dirty dishes!" "Don't be giving him any more rum!" and "I'll be fine, boys! Run for it!") and the characters say, "How does she [bloody] do that?" She acts loud and tough towards the "boys" on the surface, as shown when she threatens them with a table-scrap-free week if they forget to put out the lantern again as the previous night, but on the inside, she has a heart of gold and genuinely cares about them, as shown when she first distracts the pirates attacking the inn outside her bedroom door while Jim slips out and later while the Inn burns, she tells them to escape while she fights the intruders.
The M267 is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: WWII. It was added via an update on July 23rd, 2019.

Mysterio (real name Quentin Beck) is a Marvel Comics supervillain who appears in the 2019 Marvel Cinematic Universe film Spider-Man: Far From Home as the main antagonist. Beck posed as a superhero and allied himself with Spider-Man during the European attacks, leading to the young hero giving him E.D.I.T.H., the artificial intelligence that Tony Stark - Beck's former boss - had left for Peter, until Parker discovered that Quentin was the one who was behind the "attacks" by using realistic footage from a projector. Following the battle on the London Bridge, Beck died after being shot in the chest from a drone he was controlling, but not before making a video where he revealed, to the entire world, that Peter Parker was Spider-Man. Mysterio was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.

Never fairies are beings native to Pixie Hollow whose main function is to change the seasons on the Mainland. They are the main characters in the Disney Fairies franchise. Pixie Hollow's warm seasons are under the rule of Queen Clarion, and all warm fairies recognize her as their ruler. Alternatively, the Winter Woods are under Lord Milori's authority.

Nausicaä is a fictional character and a princess who first appeared in Studio Ghibli's 1984 theatrical release Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind, as the main protagonist. She is the princess of the Valley of the Wind, a minor kingdom in a post-apocalyptic world.
The is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare.

Pain King is one of two Pro-wrestlers which appear in the animated television show Kim Possible. He appeared in the episode "Pain King vs. Cleopatra", He is tan, strong, and tall. He has black eyes that look evil.

Penelope "Penny" Lent is a minor antagonist in Sky High. She is the school's cheerleading squad leader (in fact, the squad itself) who can multiply herself and make multiple clones to fight her enemies. She is also Gwen Grayson's best friend and becomes her henchwoman.

Robert Peabo Bryson was an American R&B and soul singer-songwriter. He was well-known for singing soul ballads and has contributed to two Disney animated feature soundtracks: Beauty and the Beast and Aladdin, both of which won him two . He also sang "As Long As There's Christmas" during the end credits of Beauty and the Beast: The Enchanted Christmas, as well as appeared in specials, like A Musical Christmas at Walt Disney World, Pocahontas: The Musical Tradition Continues, and The Hunchback of Notre Dame: Festival of Fun Musical Spectacular. He was born in Greenville, South Carolina and spent much of his childhood on his grandfather's farm in Mauldin, South Carolina. His love for music came from his mother, who often took the family to concerts of well-known African-American artists at the time. After singing with different musical groups, Byson was eventually signed to Capital Records and recorded memorable hits, such as "Feel the Fire", "Reaching for the Sky", "I'm So into You", "Crosswinds", "", "" (with Roberta Flack), "Here We Go" (with Minnie Riperton), "", "", "Closer Than Closer", and "". Bryson also recorded songs with Regina Belle, such as "", "I Can't Imagine", "Total Praise", and "A Whole New World". Bryson also performed in theater and operatic productions, most notably the tenor role of "Sportin' Life" in the Michigan Opera Theater of Detroit's version of and as Lun Tha in a studio cast recording of with Julie Andrews. The is a lever-action marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It is also briefly seen in Call of Duty: Vanguard.

Peter Cole is a character who appears in the supernatural teen drama series Coven Academy. Peter Cole is a brilliant warlock who has just transferred to Crescent Veil Academy, as an effortlessly cool new teacher. He develops a bond with Jake, offering him guidance and support.

Phantasmo, also known as Experiment 375, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to take possession of inanimate objects and, through them, create utter chaos. Being ghost-like, he is intangible and can phase through obstacles, thus making him virtually uncatchable. His one true place is keeping the Macki Macaw animatronic functional at the titular pizza restaurant.

Vance DeBar "Pinto" Colvig, Sr. was a vaudeville American actor, voice actor, comedian, newspaper cartoonist, circus performer, screenwriter, and animator, who was the story man at Walt Disney Productions, perhaps better known for his voice work. His most famous for his Disney role was as the original voice of Goofy from 1932 to 1938, and again from 1944 until his death in 1967. He also provided the voices of Pluto from 1930 to 1938 and again from 1941 to 1961, Grumpy and Sleepy in Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Practical Pig in The Three Little Pigs, and other classic characters. Born in Jacksonville, Oregon; one of seven children, he attended, but didn't graduate from Medford High School. However, Colvig was accepted and attended, sporadically from 1910 to 1913, Oregon Agricultural College, in Corvallis, where he took art classes and played clarinet in the band as well as drawing cartoons for the Oregon Agricultural College Barometer newspaper, and the yearbook. From 1913 to 1922, Colvig worked as a cartoonist and in various performances outlets including the Al G. Barnes Circus before moving his family to Hollywood. Continuing work as animator and writer for different companies, Colvig eventually obtained an eight-year contract with Walt Disney Productions as a writer and sound effects artist. Phoebe Ravenson is a recurring character in Disney Jr.'s Vampirina. She is a young witch and the eponymous girl in the episode "The Little Witch". In the episode, she and her parents visit The Scare B&B where she befriends Vampirina Hauntley, who, along with Demi and Gregoria, help her improve her witch skills so she can be as good as her parents.
Pip the Pirate Genie is a recurring character from Disney Jr.'s television series Jake and the Never Land Pirates.
Pith Possum is a Super Hero, a character and a possum, who starred in his own segment in all 13 episodes of The Shnookums and Meat Funny Cartoon Show.

The M67 Ammo is an attachment for the CR-56 AMAX assault rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It offers some benefits such as increased damage, at the cost of reduced magazine capacity and restricting the fire mode to semi-automatic.

Pop, also known as Experiment 009, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to use his tail to blow up a balloon to the size of the room he is in, then popping the balloon, discombobulating those involved near the explosion of the balloon and causing frizzy hair. He appears in the Stitch! anime.
Prince Dastan is the eponymous protagonist of Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time. He is portrayed by Jake Gyllenhaal.

Princess Charlotte is a character, who appears in the Sofia the First episode "Beauty is the Beast". She is the Princess of Isleworth, who was turned into a beast by Zinessa, her kingdom's greatest enchantress, as punishment because she had been rude and insensitive to her friend, Morris. To break the curse, Charlotte had to become true friends with Morris.
MAEVWAT Precision Industry, also simply referred to as MAEVWAT or Maevwat, is a faction and weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Mobile.
Prince Marzel is a Sirena prince, who appears in the Elena of Avalor special "Song of the Sirenas".
Quint is a muscular man with varying roles, who appears as the main antagonist in the Timon & Pumbaa TV series as the archenemy of the titular duo.
Queen Emmaline is the Mermaid Queen of Merroway Cove and the loving mother of Princesses Cora and Oona in Sofia the First.
The M91 Heavy is a barrel attachment featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Warzone. It is uniquely available to the M91 light machine gun.
Ramsley is the main antagonist of Disney's 2003 live-action fantasy comedy film The Haunted Mansion.

Ramone is a supporting character in the Disney•Pixar Cars franchise. He owns an auto body shop in Radiator Springs, which is called Ramone's House of Body Art, which is across the street from Flo's V8 Cafe. Flo is his wife. Between scenes in Cars, he would completely change the paint on his body due to lack of work in town. His basis is a 1959 Chevrolet Impala low-rider.

Raymond, simply known as Ray, is a major character in Disney's 2009 animated feature film The Princess and the Frog. He is a Cajun firefly with a romantic infatuation with the evening star, Evangeline.
The M1916 is a marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It was added as part of the Season Three update.

Remy (also known as Little Chef) is the protagonist of Disney•Pixar's 2007 animated feature film Ratatouille. He is an anthropomorphic bluish-gray rat from Paris with a passion for food who dreams of becoming a professional chef.

Reginald "Reg" Fletcher is a recurring character of the animated TV show Phineas and Ferb. He is a former daredevil known as The Flying Fishmonger. He is the grandfather of Ferb Fletcher, step-grandfather of Candace Flynn and Phineas Flynn, husband to Winifred Fletcher, and father of Lawrence Fletcher. He speaks in a heavy Leeds/British accent. As a grandfather, he suffers from many aches and pains, such as lumbago and a bad trick knee, yet he is still very spry and active as ever. His grandchildren will visit him and Winifred at least once a year, and he lives his life retired in his London home lying next to the former castle of the Black Knight of Worcestershire.

Raymond Wallace "Ray" Bolger was an American actor, singer, and dancer, who portrayed the crooked villain Barnaby in the musical film Babes in Toyland. He also appeared in an episode of Walt Disney's Wonderful World of Color ("Backstage Party") with Annette Funicello and Tommy Sands in a promotional effort for the film. Additionally, he narrated the album The Story of the Scarecrow of Oz. He was considered to voice White Rabbit in Alice in Wonderland. He was also considered for the role of Uncle Albert in Mary Poppins. Bolger began his career through vaudeville before finding work in cinema with his most famous role being the Scarecrow and farmhand Hunk in the 1939 musical film The Wizard of Oz. His other film credits included The Great Ziegfeld, Sweethearts, Rosalie, Stage Door Canteen, The Harvey Girls, April in Paris, That's Dancing!, The Daydreamer, and Where's Charley?, where he reprised his Tony Award winning role from Broadway. His other Broadway credits included Life Begins at 8:40, On Your Toes, By Jupiter, and All American. His television appearances included The Jean Arthur Show, The Partridge Family, Little House on the Prairie, Battlestar Galactica, Fantasy Island, The Love Boat, Diff'rent Strokes, and was also the host of his eponymous television show The Ray Bolger Show from 1953 and 1955, originally known as "Where's Raymond?" The (Multi-Caliber Precision Rifle-300) is a bolt-action sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. The MCPR-300 is also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.

Richard Madden is a Scottish actor. For Disney, he portrayed Kit in the 2015 live-action adaptation of Cinderella and Ikaris in Eternals. Born and raised in Elderslie near Glasgow, Madden was cast in his first role at age 11 and made his screen acting debut in 2000. He later began performing on stage whilst a student at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland. In 2007, he toured with William Shakespeare's Globe company as Romeo in Romeo and Juliet, a role he reprised in the West End theatre in 2016. With his portrayal of Robb Stark in the fantasy drama series Game of Thrones from 2011 to 2013, Madden rose to fame. His other television credits include Barmy Aunt Boomerang, Hope Springs, Medici, Bodyguard, Citadel and the miniseries Klondike. Madden also appeared in films, such as Complicity, Chatroom, Rocketman, and 1917.

Brenda (aliases Rope Girl and Funky B) is the character (voiced by Alanna Ubach) in Disney's short-lived animated Teamo Supremo. She was recruited to the team for her superb jump-roping skills, which she often makes use of in battle. She uses a special skipping rope, provided to her by Level 7 and nicknamed "Ropey" by her, to evade enemies and also capture them. The rope is also used to transform Teamo Supremo's groupies into their superhero guises. She is the only female in the titular group.

RoboGadget is an antagonist in the 1999 film Inspector Gadget. He is a completely robotic duplicate of Inspector Gadget created by Dr. Claw from his original prototype android, Prometheus. Unlike the good inspector, Robo was fitted with devices meant for death and destruction, however, he does retain the original's ability to extend his limbs. They can be told apart by his oversized white teeth and different colored clip-on tie.

The is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. It was added on August 16th, 2023 as part of the Season Five update. The M13C is also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.

Ronald Longcape Jr. is an evil kid at WizTech. He was a love interest for Alex in Season Two's "Saving WizTech: Part One" and "Saving WizTech: Part Two", while Alex was still in a relationship with Dean. Ronald shape-shifted into Dean and broke up with Alex so he could convince Alex into coming to WizTech with him; he froze the real Dean inside gelatin. Ronald then used Alex as part of his evil plan, to become the most powerful evil wizard at WizTech. His plan was foiled by Alex's love for Dean. His father, Ronald Longcape Sr. (Maurice Godin) only pretends to be evil.

Rongo the Strongo is the circus' strongman in the 2019 remake of Dumbo. Besides his duty, he also serves as Max Medici's bank accountant who helps him throughout his career in order to keep his show running.

Rudith Ray Stewart, better known by her nickname, "Mamaw" and goes by the name "Ruthie Ray Stewart", Bubba‘s wife and Robby Ray Stewart, Earl Ray Stewart and Bobby Ray Stewart‘s mother, Susan Stewart and Aunt Pearl's mother-in-law and Jackson, Miley, and Luann Stewart's paternal grandmother. She lives in Tennessee, but occasionally visits California. Ruthie is a demanding and opinionated woman, often seen nagging Robby about his habits and parenting skills. While in high school Ruthie dated fellow Tennessean Elvis Presley and claimed to have been the one to first give him the nickname "The King" after playing Checkers with him. Elvis eventually started dating Aunt Dolly which began a 30 year feud between the two women. Ruthie is also very competitive. She is a former Olympian and played volleyball at the 1964 Olympics. She even takes small games seriously, such as Battleship and Tiddlywinks. Like Robby, Ruthie has a hard time trying to accept the fact that Jackson and Miley are growing up. This is most notably seen in You Give Lunch a Bad Name and I Am Mamaw, Hear Me Roar!. Ruthie was a school lunch lady at East Northumberland High School for which she won the honor Lunch Lady of the Year from North Central Nashville School District every single year. Both Miley and Jackson love "Mamaw," but they often find her overbearing. The MCW 6.8 Full-Auto Conversion is a conversion kit for the MCW 6.8 marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Aftermarket Parts system. This kit allows the MCW 6.8 to fire in full auto, while disabling extended magazines.
Sanza is a spirit jaguar who appears in the Disney Channel animated series Elena of Avalor. He is a rouge Chanul who causes people to misbehave.

Sarah Sanderson is one of the secondary antagonists of Disney's 1993 film Hocus Pocus and its 2022 sequel, alongside her sister Mary. She is the youngest and most beautiful but air-headed witch who lived during the time of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem_witch_trials the Salem Witch Trials], along with her two sisters: Winifred and Mary. After three hundred years, Sarah and her sisters were awoken from the dead by Max Dennison and wanted to stay alive and young forever by kidnapping children and stealing their lives. She was responsible for luring children to their cottage by hypnotizing them with her singing.
The Sea Captain is a ghost who briefly appears in the Haunted Mansion.
The MK.78 is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

Scott Calvin, later Santa Claus, is the protagonist of The Santa Clause trilogy. He was an executive for a toy company before accidentally coming across the former Santa Claus, alongside his son, Charlie, and taking his place by wearing his suit. Over the year, Scott slowly became the new Santa Claus, while in denial. Scott later went on to marry Carol Newman, who took on the role as Mrs. Claus. He is Charlie, Cal and Sandra Calvin's father.

Shawn Robert Ashmore is a Canadian actor. His Disney roles so far are Cadet Major Brad Rigby in Cadet Kelly, Gord in the Flash Forward episode "Mudpack", Chet in the The Famous Jett Jackson episode "What You Wish For", Tyler Connell in In a Heartbeat, Sam Sullivan in the ABC TV show , and Wesley Evers in . Ashmore was born in Richmond, British Columbia and raised in St. Albert, Alberta and Brampton, Ontario, where he attended Earnscliffe Senior Public School and Turner Fenton Secondary School. He began acting at an early age but gain recognition as Bobby Drake/Iceman in the film series and as Jake Berenson in the television series . He has since then appeared as a guest or a lead in shows, like , , , , and TV films, like and the miniseries , where he won a for Best Lead Performance By a Male in a Feature Length Drama. His other film credits include , , , , , and .
Silver is a character from American Dragon: Jake Long. She is a mermaid who graduated Aqua Anlate Atlantis U.
The M15 Mod 0 is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

Sheeta, whose full name is Lusheeta Toel Ul Laputa ("Toel" meaning "true" and "Ul" meaning "ruler" in Laputian), is the female protagonist of Studio Ghibli's Castle in the Sky. She is a 13-year-old orphaned farm girl, whose glowing stone keeps Laputa alive.
Shujaa is an adult male gorilla, who is a member of King Sokwe's troop in The Lion Guard.

Simu Liu is a Chinese-Canadian actor, stuntman, and writer. He is best known for the role of Jung in the CBC sitcom . Liu first got his start working as an extra on Guillermo del Toro's action-sci-fi movie . For Disney, he portrayed Shang-Chi in the 2021 Marvel Cinematic Universe film Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, the 2024 Disney+ series What If...?, the 2025 Disney+ series Marvel Zombies, the 2026 film Avengers: Doomsday, the 2027 film Avengers: Secret Wars, and Shang-Chi 2. He also voiced Lah Zhima in Star Wars: Visions and Professor Lem Enall in Phineas and Ferb.
The M34 Novaline is a marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

Seth Voelker, also known as Sidewinder, is a Marvel Comics character who appears as the secondary antagonist in Captain America: Brave New World, played by Giancarlo Esposito. He is a dangerous, deadly terrorist. He is an expert marksman and deadly hand to hand combatant. He is the leader of the terrorist group known as the Serpent Society, and is hired by Samuel Sterns to take out Sam Wilson. Sidewinder was created by Mark Gruenwald, Ralph Macchio, and George Perez.

Slugger, also known as Experiment 608, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to deflect incoming enemy projectiles and swat away balls, toys, and fruits thrown over the fence by annoying kids. His one true place is at the baseball field as a coaching assistant for Little League softball.

Slimy, also known as Experiment 390, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to produce trails of slippery slime in order to trip up enemies. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".
The MK35 ISR is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It was added as part of the Season Three update.

Sinker, also known as Experiment 602, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed sink entire naval fleets with his long, razor-sharp dorsal fin; he can hold his breath underwater indefinitely to carry out his primary function. His one true place is at a Japanese restaurant, cutting up fish fillets and vegetables to make sushi.

Sir Tuxford is the highest ranking knight in King Gregor's court and his trusted friend. He is an older, jolly character, always ready for a fight but perhaps past his prime. Sir Tuxford leads the knights of Castle Dunwyn and is the main force that keeps Duke Igthorn and his Ogres away. His catchphrase is often "I'm sure I don't know, Sire." when questioned by King Gregor about the present situation. Despite his age and his appearance, Sir Tuxford has apprehended many troublemakers in Dunwyn, and done battle with Igthorn and his Ogres.
Sir Gillium is a character in Sofia the First. He is the Flying Derby Coach of the Royal Preparatory Academy.

Skylar Lewis is the main protagonist of the 2012 Disney Channel Original Movie Girl vs. Monster. A fearless teenager with a powerful voice. She gets prepared for the Ultimate Halloween bash with her best friends, Henry and Sadie. Skylar is a 16-year-old girl, who discovers that her parents are fourth generation monster hunters and she is a fifth generation monster hunter.
Slappy the Dummy is the main antagonist in the first season of Goosebumps. He is usually seen as the mascot to the franchise as a whole.

Snafu, also known as Experiment 120, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to discombobulate enemy plans by any possible means; he will also thwart any attempt to capture him, and thus can only be caught by accident.

The Snowgies (also known as Snow-Babies) are tiny, mischievous snowmen that were created by Elsa, who first appeared in the animated short Frozen Fever.

Sophie Hatter is the protagonist of Studio Ghibli's 2004 film Howl's Moving Castle. She runs a hat shop in her town along with her sisters and mother. When the Witch of the Waste curses her with a spell that turns her into a ninety-year old woman, Sophie goes to the Waste in search of a cure. She is voiced by Emily Mortimer as a young woman and Jean Simmons as an old woman.

Sosuke is the male protagonist of Ponyo. He lives on a cliff by the sea. His mother is a carer in a retirement home, and his father is a captain of a ship. He was the one to discover Ponyo. When he broke the glass in which Ponyo was stuck in, his finger was cut in the process. Ponyo licked his cut, and it immediately healed, due to her having magical powers. After taking a great liking to Ponyo, he decides to keep her and give her her name, and then he promises her to protect her forever.

The is an armored vehicle used by the US, British Commonwealth and other allies during World War II. The M3 was designed as a vehicle that would be easily steered and maneuvered, like a wheeled vehicle, but having the same off-road capabilities as a tracked vehicle.

Sonny Sonerstein is an insult stand-up comic and ghost who appeared in the episode, "Be My Ghost". He debuted his iconic rubber chicken act at a Ski Resort Hotel, and continued to regularly perform there as a ghost after it was bought out, though he left.

Sprout, also known as Experiment 509, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to sprout into an uncontrollable forest of destruction by burrowing into the ground and producing tendrils that grow replicas of his head. His one true place is atop the pineapple water tower.
Squeakers is a purple blowfish squeaky toy who communicates with squeaking noises. He can also go underwater.

Princess Star Butterfly is the titular protagonist of the Disney Channel and Disney XD animated series Star vs. the Forces of Evil. She is an intergalactic princess from the Kingdom of Mewni (located in another dimension). She is sent to Earth by her parents in order to learn how to use the Royal Magic Wand, with supervision from Glossaryck. In Seasons 1-2, she lives with her Earth hosts, the Diaz family. In Season 3, she returns home to Mewni. As of Season 4, she lives in the Monster Temple following the destruction of Butterfly Castle. She was also the 37th Queen of Mewni for four days before giving the kingdom to Eclipsa Butterfly. As of "Doop-Doop", she is back to living on Earth. From "Here to Help" onward, she is Marco Diaz's girlfriend.
Spudnick is a character who appears in Space Buddies. He is a bull terrier who flew into outer space, but desires to go home to Sasha, his owner, back in Russia.

Squire Cawker is a predatorial crow who serves as the main antagonist of the 1932 Silly Symphony, Bugs in Love. In the short, he arrives in Bugville and attempts to eat Bucky and June Bug. After trapping Bucky in a bottle, he chases June around her own home, trampling most of her furniture in the process. June shuts herself in a makeup case as Bucky frees himself. Cawker eventually grabs June, but Bucky takes a clock hand and strikes the bird multiple times. A local bug witnesses this and sounds a clock alarm to sound a militia armed with thrown-away objects. Cawker traps Bucky in a dropper when the soldiers arrive. The bugs attack him with such objects as a mousetrap and an eggbeater before finally trapping him in a shoe and forcefully feeding him castor oil. June releases Bucky and they share a passionate embrace. Squire Cawker dons a crooked top hat similar to that of the Big Bad Wolf and a vest like the one Goofy wears in his classic design.

Steve the Chameleon is a character introduced in Season 2 of the Disney animated series Phineas and Ferb.
The Sugar Plum Fairy is the creator of the Love Potion and prisoner of the Bog King in the 2015 film Strange Magic.
Susan Pevensie is the elder sister, the second eldest Pevensie child, and one of the four main protagonists of .
The M1937 ML-20 is a 152 mm howitzer used as an artillery gun by the Russians during World War II. To this date, it has only been featured in Call of Duty: World at War (Nintendo DS).

T.J. Taylor is a wizard who attended the same school as Alex, Justin, and Max. T.J. is very similar to Alex in that he uses his magic frivolously. However, unlike Alex, whose intentions are never really malicious, T.J. is not above using it to hurt people to get his own way, whether it's adding 30 years onto his ex-girlfriend's life or even brainwashing his parents so he can do whatever he wants without consequence. He is very unpopular at school, his catchphrase is "I'll show you...", something which only he thinks is funny. Sometimes, it doesn't even make sense. It is not said which of his parents is a wizard or if both were. He is in Alex's art class, which was formerly taught by his ex-girlfriend Jenny Majorheely after he turned her into a middle-aged woman out of spite (this was in the episode "Art Teacher"). In "Disenchanted Evening", he charms his parents using a noodle strudel and puts cinnamon in it to make the charm more spicy. T.J is mentioned years later in the Wizards Beyond Waverly Place episode "The Wizard at the End of the World: Part Two", along with several antagonists, as someone who could be mad at the Russo family.

Supreme Leader Snoke is one of the main antagonists of the Star Wars sequel trilogy. Snoke is the Supreme Leader of the First Order and Kylo Ren's master until the events of Star Wars: The Last Jedi, when he is betrayed by his apprentice, who chooses to kill his own master to save Rey's life. In Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker, Snoke is revealed to be an artificially humanoid alien created by the Sith Eternal and the resurrected Sheev Palpatine as part of his plan to return to power and take revenge on the Skywalkers, thus creating Snoke to seduce Ben Solo to the dark side and rule the First Order in his stead while the Sith Eternal’s fleet, the Final Order, is being built on Exegol.

Swordsman (real name Jacques "Jack" Duquesne) is a Marvel Comics character who debuted in the Marvel Cinematic Universe in the Disney+ series Hawkeye. He is a wealthy socialite who was Kate Bishop's prime suspect in the murder of Armand Duquesne III and was later framed by Eleanor Bishop for money laundering. Swordsman was created by Stan Lee and Don Heck.

The MAT-49 is a submachine gun that appears in Call of Duty: Black Ops DS. It has a 32 round magazine and has a high rate of fire with little recoil. It appears as a Soviet used SMG, along with the PPSh-41 and the PPS-43. It is found in the later levels of the campaign used by the Red Army. It is unlocked after 150 kills with the Makarov PM, and 150 kills with the MAT-49 will unlock the PPS-43. It can also be found in the Mystery Box in Zombies mode.

Tabitha "Tabi", Teresa "Tere", and Antoñia "Toñita" Ramirez (collectively known as the T Sisters) are supporting characters in the 2024 Disney Channel animated series Primos. They are a trio of sisters who are always showing off their acrobatic set and dream of being stars in the future.

Technovore is a nanotech A.I. in the form of a large mechanical parasite that consumes any data, machinery, and energy itself in The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes. Technovore was created by Len Kaminski and Kevin Hopgood.
Tazama is a character featured in The Lion Guard. She is a former member of the Outsiders and the current keenest of sight in the Lion Guard under Vitani.

The MP40 (Maschinenpistole 40) is a German submachine gun. It is the most frequently featured submachine gun in the Call of Duty franchise, as it is featured in all World War II installments, as well as appearing in most main games of the Black Ops series and in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It also makes a brief appearance in the Call of Duty: Mobile comics.

Terence is one of the male protagonists from the Disney Fairies films. He is a dust-keeper sparrow man and Tinker Bell's best friend. He is romantically infatuated towards Tinker Bell. However, she is oblivious of this.

He is an extremely violent criminal with a metal claw on his left hand, who was eventually hypnotized into being a law abiding citizen. He was voiced by Frank Welker, in a tone very similar to that of his character Dr. Claw from the original Inspector Gadget cartoon.

The Bug Master is a villain from the animated series Darkwing Duck. Her real name is Bianca Beakley, a former newscaster and Gosalyn Mallard's role model. To boost ratings, Bianca became a villain and started to commit crimes by controlling insects in the episode "Fraudcast News". She was voiced by April Winchell.

The Fly Brothers are minor antagonists in Disney•Pixar's 1998 animated feature film A Bug's Life.

The Gardeners (formerly known as The Garden Fairies) are minor characters from Disney's 2022 animated/live-action feature film, Disenchanted. They are Giselle and Robert Philip’s gardeners. When they are infected by Giselle’s wish to live a fairytale life and Monroeville turns into Monrolasia, they are transformed into fairies.
The Mage (voiced by B.J. Ward) is a supporting character and antihero from the W.I.T.C.H. animated series.

The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified, and Call of Duty Online. It was also cut from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and appears as an MP5 modification in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare.

The Scorpion is the sole antagonist of Honey, I Shrunk the Kids. He is a tiny red one living in the Szalinskis' backyard. Though small, he was huge when the kids were shrunk to 1/4 of an inch tall. His gender is unrevealed, but it is presumed his gender is male.
Theodore "Ted" Pauley is a character in the 2001 Disney/Pixar animated film, Monsters, Inc.. He is a large hulking monster who works for Monsters, Incorporated.

Tickle-Tummy, also known as Experiment 275, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. She is designed to tickle anyone into submission, rendering opponents helpless with laughter; they sometimes even cause an accident in the process. She was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".
The is a weapon that appears as a machine pistol in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and as a submachine gun in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

Thistle is a garden fairy, who appeared in Prize Prilla's Prize. She won the carrot toss on the Great Games, while Prilla Prilla couldn't even pick up a small carrot. She appears as a main character in Tinker Bell to the Rescue, in it, she has a crush on the dust keeper, Jerome. She was first mentioned in Beck and the Great Berry Battle, when they say that a raccoon had trampled through her garden.

Toby Tortoise is one of the titular characters of the Silly Symphony, The Tortoise and the Hare and Toby Tortoise Returns. He is the primary rival of speedy Max Hare, but he finds a way to beat him by taking his time. He also makes a cameo appearance in the 1988 Touchstone Pictures/Amblin entertainment film, Who Framed Roger Rabbit. He was voiced by Eddie Holden. Although he didn't appear in Mickey Mouse Works, his name was mentioned on a punch card in "Donald's Rocket Ruckus". In House of Mouse, Toby Tortoise often appears as a guest seated at a table with Max Hare applauding between cartoons. Toby appeared in various episodes including "Timon and Pumbaa", "Rent Day", and "Thanks to Minnie". Toby is often represented musically by a slow theme played on a slap tongue bass clarinet.

Anthony Frank "Tony" Hawk, nicknamed "The Birdman", is an American actor, professional skateboarder, and entrepreneur. A pioneer of modern vertical skateboarding, Tony Hawk completed the first documented "900" skateboarding trick at the X Games in 1999. He also licensed published by that same year. He retired from competition in 2003 and is regarded as one of the most influential skateboarders of all time. Tony Hawk has been involved in various philanthropic activities throughout his career. He is also the founder of the Tony Hawk Foundation (now named ), which helps to build skateparks in underprivileged areas around the world. For Disney, he made a cameo in Max Keeble's Big Move and guest-starred in the Phineas and Ferb spin-off Take Two with Phineas and Ferb. He also appeared as himself in an episode of The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, and voiced Hush in Kick Buttowski: Suburban Daredevil and Jagger/Allen in Big City Greens. Additionally, Tony's eponymous series formed the basis of Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure, which notably reused the engine and mechanics from while introducing simplified controls and characters from the Disney and Pixar franchises. Mr. Hawk was one of the interviewed subjects in the 2002 Touchstone Pictures and ESPN Films production Ultimate X: The Movie. Additionally, he served as inspiration for the movement of Tarzan in the film of the same name.

The is an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) used primarily by the USAF and CIA. The MQ-1 is used as an all-purpose UAV, performing reconnaissance on ground targets and/or attacking. The MQ-1 is featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare: Mobilized and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.

Tubby is a red-haired, overweight kindergartener. His main duty in his kindergarten class is to chase big kids out from among them. The big kids have no trouble escaping him because he is so slow. He can produce the best burps in 3rd Street except for the brief time when Jared Smith, who could burp better than Tubby, moved there.
Troyo is a supporting antagonist in the Disney Jr. series, Elena of Avalor. He was an evil magical coyote who is a longtime enemy of the Jaquins.

Twitch is a strangling who appears in the Disney Jr. animated series Sofia the First. He is a shapeshifter and can change into any animal he wishes, although his default form appears to be a rat.

Ursula is a character who appears in ABC's fantasy series Once Upon a Time. She is the daughter of Poseidon's and a former member of the Queens of Darkness. She is based on the character of the same name from Disney's 1989 film The Little Mermaid.

The MPL is a submachine gun which appears in the Multiplayer and Zombies modes of Call of Duty: Black Ops.

Whirlybird (or simply Whirly) is Oso's talking helicopter in Special Agent Oso who takes Oso to someplace where someone needs help. He can't hear very well and often misunderstands what Oso tells him, which usually leads to Oso's ejection at inopportune moments and places.

Whitehood is the main antagonist of the Jungle Cubs episode "Treasure of the Middle Jungle". According to legend as told by Bagheera, he is a giant poisonous cobra who guards the treasure of the Middle Jungle's temple from Man and other sort of trespassers.

William Turner, better known as Will Turner, is a main character of the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise. Born as the son of Bootstrap Bill, a father he did not know was a pirate, Will Turner remains humble and selfless even as he sails the seas to save his father and find his true love Elizabeth Swann. In his life, Will Turner was an accomplished blacksmith by trade, an excellent swordsman by pursuit and a budding pirate by fate. After Elizabeth was kidnapped by Captain Barbossa aboard the Black Pearl, Will joined forces with Captain Jack Sparrow to save her while being pursued by Commodore Norrington's men and facing cursed pirates. After embarking on several adventures with Sparrow, Will embraced his pirate heritage as he pursued his own purposes. About a year later, Will and Elizabeth were tricked into helping Jack find the Dead Man's Chest. This led Will aboard Davy Jones's ship, the Flying Dutchman, where Will met up with his father, Bootstrap Bill. Will promised Bill that he'd try and free him from Jones' servitude. Despite his best efforts, Will would try and do everything he could to honor that vow, but not forgetting that he still loved Elizabeth. This led to Will and Elizabeth being married during the final battle against Beckett's Armada. Shortly after being stabbed by Jones, Will himself pierced Jones' heart, thereby becoming the new captain of the Dutchman. Magic Wrench is a cut Vehicle Perk from Call of Duty: World at War. Its exact function is unknown, but based on it's name and emblem it could possibly allow players to repair damaged Tanks.
Wilbur is a supporting character in Disney's 1990 animated feature film The Rescuers Down Under. He is the older brother of Orville from the first film.
Wilby Daniels is the protagonist of the first Shaggy Dog movies. He is transformed into an Old English Sheepdog by saying magic words on a ring that belonged to the Borgias.

Windlifter is a major character in the 2014 Disneytoon Studios animated feature film Planes: Fire & Rescue. He is a big green helicopter who's the second-in-command of the Piston Peak Air Attack team.

The is an unmanned aerial vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. The Reaper appears to be the successor to the Predator drone from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.

Wizard Kelly is a recurring foil in Disney Channel's The Proud Family. He is the ambiguously moral celebrity that is a constant reminder of Oscar Proud's failures. While not necessarily an antagonist in the traditional sense, he tends to act as an obstacle for Penny Proud and her friends.

Wrapper, also known as Experiment 521, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to mummify individuals in tape. His one true place is with Mrs. Hasagawa as one of her "cats".

Wolfman is a minor character from The Nightmare Before Christmas. He is a werewolf and a resident of Halloween Town. Compared most other residents of the town, Wolfman enjoys Halloween and spooky events, and even helps Jack make Christmas theirs.

The is a bladed melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, and a Campaign Scorestreak in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It also makes brief appearances in Call of Duty: World at War, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Ghosts and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare.

The Yeti, or the "Abominable Snowman", is a cryptid said to live in the Himalayas of Central Asia. It has appeared in various Disney media, most prominently in the theme parks and is usually depicted as a ferocious territorial beast. The most well known and recurring Disney incarnation of the creature is the one from the Matterhorn Bobsleds attraction at Disneyland, known by the nickname of Harold.

The Yautja (commonly referred to as the Predators or Hunters) are an extraterrestrial species that appear in the franchise as the main antagonists and, at times, as anti-heroes. They are a sentient humanoid race known for hunting dangerous species for sport and honor.

Yen Sid is a character that first appeared the 1940 Disney animated feature film Fantasia. Appearing in the The Sorcerer's Apprentice segment, he is a sorcerer that served as Mickey Mouse's mentor in the art of magic.

The Remington MSR is a bolt-action sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty Online. It also makes a cameo appearance Call of Duty: Ghosts, and was cut from Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.
Xerxes is the familiar of the sorcerer Mozenrath. He is a floating eel/lamprey-like creature, who speaks in broken English. He appears in the Aladdin TV series.

Zazu is a major character in Disney's 1994 animated feature film The Lion King. He is an uptight, red-and-yellow-billed hornbill who served as King Mufasa's majordomo. Zazu is charged with upholding order within the Pride Lands, though he is rarely taken seriously due to his diminutive size and fragile temper.
Zinessa is a character who appears in the Sofia the First episode "Beauty is the Beast". She is the kingdom of Isleworth's greatest enchantress.
Marine Camouflage is a type of weapon camouflage found in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.

He thinks highly of himself and he is a descendant of the ancients. He is also a distant cousin of Merlon and Merlee. He is responsible for granting Mario the ability to switch between the second and third dimensions, an ability that the game showcases throughout the entire story. His name is a pun on the word "bestow", as he bestows upon Mario the ability to flip between dimensions. It may also be a pun on "best of us", due to his arrogant personality. He is also a distant cousin of Merlon and Merlee, and is a direct cousin of Old Man Watchitt. According to Bestovius, he no longer needs it because he got a newer, sleeker model. Bestovius believes that people from another dimension can listen to him, and also that they would wish to know that Mario can flip dimensions with . Electro Koopa is an enemy which only appears in Super Mario Sunshine. They are a variant of a Koopa with an electrified shell.

Big Whomps are a larger sized species Whomps, first seen in New Super Mario Bros.. They are rather rare types of Whomps, having only three appearances. They are similar to Big Thwomps, as they can also break through Brick Blocks.
The MSMC (also known as the Mini INSAS in the game files) is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Black Ops III and Call of Duty: Mobile.

]] Blumiere's father was a member of the Tribe of Darkness. Little is known about the father, and he is only mentioned in a few of Blumiere's backstory segments in Super Paper Mario. Blumiere's father did not accept the love his son expressed for the human, Lady Timpani, since marrying anyone outside of the tribe was forbidden out of fear that their powerful magic bloodline would become diluted (as explained by Carson). Upon learning that the two lovers were planning to elope, Blumiere's father stopped their marriage by using his magic powers to curse Timpani to wander the dimensions until the day she died. Losing Timpani spurred Blumiere to steal the Dark Prognosticus from the care of his tribe so that he could destroy the world that took his love away. Blumiere's father begged him to stop, but Blumiere, now calling himself Count Bleck, killed him and wiped out the rest of the Tribe of Darkness as the first step towards destroying the world. Although Blumiere's father does not make a physical appearance in Super Paper Mario, his silhouette appears in the game's adaptation in Super Mario-kun. He is depicted as a heavyset figure with a large mustache, and wears what resembles a bowler hat.

A Bow Balloon (ボウバルーン, Bō Barūn) is an enemy in Wario Land 4. They are Vikings that are armed with bows. They will attack by firing an arrow if they spot Wario, turning him in his puffy form. de:Bow Balloon

The Bog Monster is an apparently horrific creature that, according to Klump, eats everything in sight. They reside in the Forbidden Forest on Kongo Bongo Island in the Donkey Kong Country cartoon. In the Donkey Kong Country episode "Bug A Boogie", it is revealed that Donkey Kong secretly feared the Bog Monster, as, when he was young, Cranky Kong told him that if he ventured into the Forbidden Forest, the Bog Monster would get him; one day, Donkey Kong disobeyed Cranky Kong and decided to go into the Forbidden Forest, only to encounter and subsequently be scared by a Bog Monster. It is later revealed to Donkey Kong by Cranky Kong that he had, in actuality, simply made up the story of the Bog Monster, and that it was him who scared Donkey Kong when he entered the Forbidden Forest, wanting to teach Donkey Kong a lesson in disobeying him. Oddly, it seems the Bog Monster may have been an actual creature, as, at the end of "Bug A Boogie", Klump and Krusha, while trying to help King K. Rool out of a pit of quicksand he was stuck in, hear a monstrous roar in the Forbidden Forest, seemingly the Bog Monster. Diddy Kong also has the unique talent of mimicking the roar of one.
The is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II and Call of Duty Online.

Bowser the Brash is the Old West-style alter-ego of Bowser. He is the villain of Western Land in Mario Party 2. The outlaw wears a cowboy hat. At the end of the Western Land party, the winning player must save a Koopa Troopa banker from Bowser the Brash. A duel with pop-cork guns is fought to save the money.
Briers are floating creatures that are covered in spikes. They only appear in Yoshi Touch & Go.
Butatabi (ぶたたび) are enemies in Wario Land 4. They are pigs drawn and brought to life by Hoggus. Butatabi glide from right to left, attacking with the spike on its forehead.

The Manual Crossbow is a secondary Special weapon available in the campaign mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It uses the same model as the Crossbow from Call of Duty: Black Ops; albeit the only difference is that the Manual Crossbow has no attachments and some differences in the color. The Manual Crossbow can only shoot explosive tip bolts and cannot switch to ordinary bolts unlike in the previous game. It is unlocked by completing five challenges in the campaign mission "Karma".

Cat Boomerang Bros. are a variant of Boomerang Bro featured in the Bowser's Fury mode of Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury. They are among the cat enemy variants, and Cat Boomerang Bros. resemble a Boomerang Bro but have cat ears and a tail. de:Katzen-Bumerang-Bruder
Cat Magikoopas are a cat variant of Magikoopa and an enemy in the Bowser's Fury campaign of Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury.

Captain Olimar (or simply Olimar) is the main protagonist of the Pikmin franchise, created by Shigeru Miyamoto. Olimar is actually named after Mario himself (Olimar is an anagram of Mario, with an L added; his Japanese name, Orimā, (オリマー) which was romanized as Olimar, is a near perfect anagram of "Mario"). He has crossed over with the Mario franchise primarily through the Super Smash Bros. series, but also through Nintendo Land as well, where Pikmin gets its own attraction, titled "Pikmin Adventure." Most of his other appearances involve cameos via amiibo. Olimar had to be scaled up drastically, even more so than Kirby, for his appearance in the Super Smash Bros. series, as according to the Pikmin game manual, he is only about an inch tall. Olimar does not have any voice effects (unless players count his whistles as a voice effect) in Super Smash Bros. Brawl, making him the only playable character in the game without a star KO sound effect (although he would later share this trait with other characters in future installments). However, in Pikmin 2, Pikmin 3, and Super Mario Maker, he is voiced by Kazumi Totaka. In Super Smash Bros. games beginning with Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS onward, Alph, one of the protagonists of Pikmin 3, appears as an alternate costume of Olimar. Cosmic Luigi is very similar to his counterpart with the only difference being is that he long jumps a lot, and takes shortcuts, making him bit harder to beat than Cosmic Mario however he does show a few weaknesses in the race such as accidentally slipping into honey, taking longer routes allowing you to slip right past him if he's beating you. Croakaokes are squat duck-like creature with leaves on their heads found in various chapters in Yoshi and the Mysterious book. They sing notes when Yoshi bounces on their heads to get higher.

Dr. Toby appears in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Super Plant". Dr. Toby is a somewhat absent-minded, yet friendly doctor, who possesses the superhuman ability to sense whenever a plant is dying. When the basil plant belonging to Mama Mario (which Mario and Luigi were looking after) is dying, Dr. Toby can sense it and comes running over to Mario Brothers Plumbing to help. Dr. Toby presents Mario and Luigi with his experimental Super Plant Growth Formula, which he claims would be able to save the basil bush, and warns them to follow the instructions before leaving. At some point later, Dr. Toby is called by Mario, who reports that his plant formula worked, but ends up transforming the basil bush into Super Plant that is attacking Luigi. Dr. Toby tries to give Mario some advice over the phone, but has to ultimately return to the basement with an antidote for the formula, which he uses to shrink Super Plant back down to its original basil bush form. As an apology, Dr. Toby then offers the Mario Bros. his new fast-acting Super Yeast formula to use in their pizza dough, but they quickly refuse his offer.
The MP5 is a submachine gun featured in many games of the Modern Warfare series, as well as in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War.

A Dull Bones is a chartreuse variant of Dry Bones first seen in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. They resemble Dry Bones but are implied to've been skeletons much longer, as a result, their bones have become more stale. Due to this, Dull Bones are often weaker and more fragile than a regular Dry Bones however some of their appearance have inverted this making the Dull Bones stronger despite their fragile nature.

The Gold Koopeleon is a rare, shining golden variant of the regular Koopeleon that appears as an enemy in Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time. Like their species origin, Gold Koopeleons have the ability to turn nearly invisible, but will flee from Mario, Luigi and their baby counterparts in the overworld. Gold Koopeleons can be found in the Thwomp Caverns.
The Hanabihei is an enemy from Super Mario Bros. Wonder. They are a variation of the Bob-omb.
The is a marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Holly Mackerel is a mermaid in The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "The Ugly Mermaid." She is the princess of the underwater land of Mertropolis, and the daughter of King Mackerel. During the episode, Mario is entombed in concrete by King Koopa and drowns by being sent to the sea floor, but is saved by Holly, who takes him to Mertropolis. Princess Toadstool, Luigi and Toad follow them. After rescuing Mario, Holly falls in love with him, mistaking him for a frog prince. Her name is a portmanteau of "Holly," a given female name, and "holy mackerel," an expression of surprise. Unlike traditional depictions of mermaids, she has female human legs and a fish's head and torso.

Hildy is a witch-like woman and an apparent inhabitant of Rotundaland, whose ruler, Queen Rotunda, she appears to be friends with. She appears in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Love 'Em and Leave 'Em".

Hunky Chunky (Kremlinous Churshum) is a special ability used by Chunky Kong in the game Donkey Kong 64. Chunky can purchase the potion containing this move from Cranky's Lab around the same time he can purchase the Primate Punch.

The Marksman Rifle, also known as DMR (Designated Marksman Rifle), is a class of rifles seen in Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Vanguard, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It is a hybrid class between Sniper Rifles and Assault Rifles. Weapons in the class are usually semi-automatic, but some of them are bolt-action. In Ghosts, the semi-automatic Marksman Rifles can often be modified with the Burst Fire attachment to fire in three-round burst mode. All Marksman Rifles in Ghosts have sluggish handling speeds. Marksman Rifles are unique in that all of the Marksman Rifles are equipped with a scope. This scope reduces recoil by 15%, via placing a 0.85x multiplier on the recoil profile . Other optical attachments do not have the same effect on the Marksman Rifles. Unlike Sniper Rifles, Marksman Rifles have a large array of optical attachments, including their unique Iron Sights. The Aim Down Sights time is 300 milliseconds, and the hip-fire cone is very large, comparable to that of a Light Machine Gun. All Marksman Rifles, bar the MR-28, have a magazine capacity of 18, making the ammunition loadout of 56 rounds somewhat limited. Most Marksman Rifles also reload at a subpar rate. Melon Piranha Plant is a variant of Piranha Plant introduced in Super Mario Bros. Wonder. It is capable of spitting watermelon seeds, much like in the series, where a Yoshi can spit watermelon seeds while a watermelon is in its mouth. Mario can stomp on the seeds that these creatures spit without taking damage. Melon Piranha Plants have a head pattern that makes their head resemble a watermelon due to having thick, dark green squiggly lines, which alongside the seeds they spit is how these creatures got their name. de:Melonen-Piranha-Pflanze ja:スイカパックン
Miss Warps (also called Mr. Warps in an issue of Nintendo Power and Sleeping Warps in an issue of the ) are helpful round egg-like characters found in Yoshi's Story.

The Ninjohn is an enemy in Super Paper Mario. Its name is a pun on the word "ninja" and the common name "John". It looks like a Ninjoe but it is green, faster, and often throws many ninja stars at the player and has more of a chance to become a decoy. They also deal more damage to the player. Ninjohns are found assisting Sammer Guys in Sammer's Kingdom, and on their own in the Flipside Pit of 100 Trials. They are also very fast and can prove a nuisance when dealing with the Sammer Guys. Taking out the Ninjohn first is the best strategy. Ninjohn is never fought during the main story, as they first appear during the 56th Sammer Guy round. Ten Sammer Guys are assisted by a Ninjohn: #56, #63, #66, #69, #71, #76, #81, #89, #93, and #94. There is no solid strategy to defeat it, though stunning it with Fleep and then jumping on it or using Barry to reflect the ninja stars works effectively.
The is a bullpup three-round burst assault rifle that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts.
Swampires are a variant of Swooper featured as an enemy in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door.

A Topmini (also called a Mini Topman) is a type of Topman, and is the smallest of the bunch It makes its first appearance in Super Mario Galaxy and reappears in Super Mario Galaxy 2. They don't have any weapons to hurt Mario but makes him spin and push him around.

Young Cricket and his martial arts teacher, Master Mantis, are a duo in the . Both of them first appear in WarioWare: Smooth Moves. Both of them are martial artists, with Young Cricket being a devoted student of Master Mantis's. The two of them are employees for WarioWare, Inc..
The MTAR-X is a bullpup weapon appearing as a submachine gun in Call of Duty: Ghosts and as an assault rifle in Call of Duty Online.

Brash is the athletic member of the Brothers Bear. He appears in Donkey Kong Country 3: Dixie Kong's Double Trouble!, where he owns a cabin (changed to a stadium in the remake) in the northwest end of Kremwood Forest. He is a jock with a mohawk and a stopwatch around his neck, wearing an angry expression unlike the other bears. Brash held a record of completing Riverside Race in one minute and 15 seconds for two years, which he brags about to Dixie and Kiddy Kong, but the Kongs manage to beat his record, Brash throws a powerful tantrum that causes a nearby log to fall into the riverbank on the Kremwood Forest map, forming a bridge leading into the secret cave, Arich's Hoard. When subsequently visiting Brash, he stays mad at the Kongs, even insisting that they leave. Brash wears a different outfit in the game's artwork that contains the Rare logo next to the words "Rarebare", a clear pun on the company's title. In addition to this artwork, the Nintendo Player's Guide also contains mirrored artwork where the Rare logo is removed and the logo is renamed to "Rare Bear". In the remake, Brash's outfit was changed to a blue headband, a white undershirt, and blue sweatpants with a white stripe. He is no longer wearing a stopwatch.

Bwaluigi is a notable Rabbid enemy in Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle. As his name suggests, he is similar to Waluigi, with similar height, cap, and clothes, although he is bulky rather than skinny, even more so than his ally Bwario. His artwork incorrectly depicts him with bright blue overalls; however, in the game itself he wears the proper blackish blue-colored overalls. Bwaluigi appears in the Lava Pit, apparently created by the Megabug to stop the heroes' advance on Bowser's Castle. He is fought twice (outside challenges); the first time alongside the weaker Bwario, and the second time alongside both Bwario and the Lava Queen. Bwaluigi behaves much like a Smasher; charging at the heroes (both on his turn and after being attacked with ranged weapons) in an attempt to hit them with the large red pipe he uses as a bludgeon. This can also inflict the Honey status on a critical, leading to heroes being stuck next to him, allowing him to hit them multiple times. Bwaluigi also has the same sounds as a Smasher. In addition to significantly more HP than most enemies (and even some bosses), Bwaluigi can force characters towards him with his Magnet Dance Technique, possibly making them vulnerable to attack (even more vulnerable if Bwario's Villain Sight is active and he is near Bwaluigi). Bwaluigi can use this Technique without cooldown if he is not Frozen or under the Stone Super Effect during his turn. He and all of his allies must be defeated to claim victory, except during the L

Burnadette is the princess of the Skorcheen people in Mario & Luigi: Brothership. She is the romantic partner and later wife of Chilliam, the prince of the Slippenglide people. She is a rotund Concordian woman with orange skin and red hair wearing a brown and orange dress. She has a flame on her head like the rest of her people, with hers being in the shape of a crown. Her name is a portmanteau of "burn" and the feminine name "Bernadette".
The MP11 is a submachine gun that appears in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.

__NOTOC__ Carry Aliens are enemies in Princess Peach: Showtime!, and are associates of the Sour Bunch. They are giant, cephalopoid extraterrestrials with purple bodies and tentacles, and lavender-gray mantles with an antenna on top. They appear chiefly in the alien invasion plays, first showing up in Mighty Mission: Alien Invasion, where a Carry Alien relentlessly chases after several Theets and keeps them captured above its head with ring beams pulsing from its antenna, who upon defeat is followed up by a second Carry Alien. Mighty Peach is required to hit a Carry Alien three times to defeat it and free its captive Theets. In Dark Space & the Great Meteor, one Carry Alien succeeds in capturing the Professor during the rescue mission to save the Mighty Sparkla. Carry Aliens also appear in the Mighty Rehearsal, where Mighty Peach must rescue as many Theets from them and the Enban Gata UFO within the time limit.

Chanchako's mother is a whale that was trapped in the ice of Tetris Shima in the Super Mario Land 3 manga, essentially becoming the inner structure of the entire island. Her only distinctive traits are long eyelashes and big lips. While Mario, Luigi, and Peach are sailing to Tetris Shima, they encounter Chanchako, the whale's child, that is looking for someone to help him free his from the ice of Tetris Shima and leads them there. After the group defeats King Tetris, the ice of the island breaks, freeing Chanchako's mother, and she sends the King flying with her blowhole, making him lose his mask and book, the prizes he promised to Mario in case he won. After retrieving both prizes, the whales bid farewell to Mario and his friends and go to their separate ways.

Cave Troopas are a prehistoric variation of Koopa Troopas. They appear in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Quest for Pizza", and serve as the minions of Alley Koop. In "Quest for Pizza", Cave Troopas appear when Alley Koop orders them to attack Luigi, Princess Toadstool, and Toad after Mario becomes unconscious from getting bitten by his Cobrat. Their main method of attacking is either throwing their spears, or launching said spears by using bows. Later, when Luigi and his friends venture to find a Fire Flower to cook Mario's pizza, the Cave Troopas launch their spears at Luigi until he grabs the Fire Flower and transforms into Super Luigi, in which they retreat afterwards.
The MR23 is a semi-automatic rifle appearing as an assault rifle in Call of Duty Online and as a marksman rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

Chilliam is the prince of the Slippenglide people and Burnadette's lover and later husband in Mario & Luigi: Brothership. He is a tall, lanky man with blue skin and icy hair. His name is a portmanteau of "chill" and the masculine name "William".

Choropūko is a female Mega Monty Mole with lipstick and fangs that appears in volume 23 of Super Mario-kun. When Mario, Yoshi and Toad putt golf balls into her home, Choropūko comes up and tells them to stop. She then proceeds to throw small rocks at them. Mario tries going back to her home to defeat her, but Mario is shocked when she pulls out a massive boulder to throw at them. Mario then kicks Choropūko in the mouth. She then drops the boulder on Mario and his friends, then proceeding to claw up Mario as well. Toad then proceeds to pull out a Super Star that Mario uses to power up his Golf Club. Mario putts many golf balls at Choropūko, but her children manage to catch the golf balls (though some get hit by them). She starts crying, telling Mario and his friends to not hurt her children, which makes Mario and his friends leave as Choropūko and her children say goodbye.

Chōchin Unkō is a minor antagonist that only appears in chapter 3 of Super Mario-kun Volume 10. It is a shaped like feces. While swimming in Pukupuku Kai, Mario and Bowser-Wanda's heads are attached with a small octopus and a respectively, hindering them. Taking advantage of this, the Chōchin Unkō approaches and attacks them with its light, which slowly turns them faces-shaped. To save his friends, Yoshi eats them, digesting the two fishes on their heads and laying his friends in an egg. Without the octopus draining his energy, Mario is able to defeat the Chōchin Unkō with a fireball.
Magma Camouflage is a weapon camouflage in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare and Call of Duty: Mobile.
Cookatiel Showdown! is the fifth and final story mission of the Luncheon Kingdom in Super Mario Odyssey. The mission's objective is to defeat Cookatiel.

Crumples is an elderly Blockafeller who appears in Yoshi's Crafted World. He wears an elf hat and holds a cane. Crumples appears twice in the game. He is first found after Yoshi completes the level The Tin-Can Condor at Big Paper Peak. Crumples informs Yoshi that three Dream Gems landed in different areas, with the world map going into branching paths. He appears again after Yoshi completes the level Gator Train Attacks! in Rumble Jungle. He does not let Yoshi continue to Outer Orbit until the orange, yellow, and magenta Dream Gems are obtained. Each time he leaves, Crumples has balloons come out of his back and he floats away. A Crumples costume can also be randomly obtained in Hidden Hills for 300 Coins.

The Crudwurm is a massive, bipedal creature that appears in Yoshi and the Mysterious Book. It is a blue, skeletal creature that covers itself with dirt. It is only encountered in Chapter 7: Underground in the Crudwurm Domain, which is unlocked by completing the Billeau Habitat. Crudwurm appears when Kamek and Bowser Jr. are talking with Yoshi and ends up capturing the former two, rendering them petrified within its shell. As such, Yoshi must fight the giant beast to free the duo.
The Magnetron is a directed-energy heavy weapon featured in the Exo Zombies map Infection from the Ascendance DLC of Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.

Daisy, more formally known as Princess Daisy, is the princess of Sarasaland and a recurring character in the Super Mario franchise. She is an energetic and tomboyish princess. Mario once saved her and her kingdom from the rule of Tatanga in 1989's Super Mario Land on the Game Boy. Daisy would not make a major appearance again until Mario Tennis on the Nintendo 64 in 2000, and she has since made relatively frequent appearances in games of various genres. She is Luigi's love interest and Princess Peach's best friend. Daisy's traits and abilities are often flower-based.

The Dark Ninja is a boss appearing in Princess Peach: Showtime! He is a Ninja Dūke who is imbued with dark powers from Grape and is part of the Sour Bunch. Appearing as the boss in The Dark Ninja & the Legion of Guards, he initially appears as a red Mihari Musha that guards the captured Ninja Sparkla, before Ninja Peach defeated him, only fully revealing himself to them halfway through the level. Peach and the Ninja Sparkla work their way through a labyrinth of traps and perils, catching up to him and taking him out. The Dark Ninja has similarities with a red-clad Ninja Dūke from the level Ninjutsu: The Art of Rapids. Like the Dark Ninja, this Ninja Dūke was disguised as a red Mihari Musha that guarded the Scholar prior to Ninja Peach defeating him, and appears as the final opponent of the play that Peach must chase down in an auto-run segment.

Dousi is an original character that appears in the Super Mario Land manga adaptation in the Super Mario series from KC Deluxe. He is a (a Taoist priest) who lives in the Chai Kingdom temple with his pupil Nankin and his daughter Minmei. He walks around with a staff that has a hand on it; the hand is open in the story, but makes a peace gesture in the character list. After his student saves Mario and Mecha Kuribō from a pack of Pionpi, he leads them to the temple, where Dousi explains how Tatanga cursed the Kingdom, turning the citizens into Pionpi, while the rest were bitten by the infected and turned into Pionpi. They were spared due to a magic seal they used as a door latch, preventing the Pionpi to enter. Dousi also suggests that, in order to reach Tatanga's base on top of the mountain, Mario would need to use the Sky Pop, which Dousi used to fly in his youth and would never let anyone use unless they were able to put their thumb and index finger to good use, so he tests Mario. Later, a Goombo manages to enter the temple and destroy the seal, letting the Pionpi inside. Dousi hears the commotion and sees his student and daughter being bitten. He then orders Mario to run to the airport with a new seal made by Mecha Kuribō, before his infected student and daughter barge in and bite him. The Main Battle Tank is a non-playable tank seen in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare and Call of Duty: Mobile.
Fishing Boos (alternatively Fishin' Boos) are ghostly Fishin' Lakitus that ride a cloud without a face. They attempt to hit the player character with a blue flame at the end of their fishing lines.

Gassox (originally named Mokura; incorrectly called Mokuka in its battle message) is a green gaseous entity in Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars and its remake that lives in Land's End and later at Belome Temple, acting as an optional boss. When engaged in battle, Gassox resembles a green cloud with two eyes and a mouth. However, outside of battle, Gassox resembles a small white puff of smoke. When in this form, Gassox wanders around Land's End, randomly appearing in different areas and running away from attackers. If an adventurer can chase down Gassox, a battle begins. When the battle begins, Gassox will be invisible and assume the name Formless. Since Gassox is invisible, the creature can dodge all regular attacks. However, Formless cannot dodge special attacks. Since Formless has no magic defense and low HP, it can be taken down with the simplest special attacks. Formless can use a variety of magical attacks, including Bolt, Static Electricity, Electroshock, and Solidify. Once a special attack is used against Formless, the cloud creature will assume its true form, the green Gassox. Gassox will retain all of the magic attacks it used during its Formless state. In its gaseous state, Gassox is weak against regular attacks and strong against special attacks. After defeating Gassox, the party will earn 30 Experience Points. Bowser summons Gassox whenever he uses his Poison Gas attack.

The Ghosts of Christmas are characters that appear in the German Club Nintendo comic "Warios Weihnachtsmärchen". They are based on the ghosts in Charles Dickens' , and they serve the same function: making the main character of the story (Wario) aware of his bad behavior in order to turn them into a better person.

Madman is a character in Call of Duty Online in Cyborg Evacuation whom the players must rescue. He is one of the three NPCs that carry a weapon and can shoot back at the cyborgs, along with Sergeant and Trigger. His hidden item is a pair of Akimbo Rangers, despite Madman carrying a Model 1887.

Genshi Yoshi is Yoshi's ancestor from the Jurassic Era, who appears in the "Time Traveler" storyline of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. He was the one to discover that the Yoshi-kind is able to swallow prey bigger than himself. He looks just like Yoshi, with his only (occasional) distinctive traits being a with「ジャストミート」(jasuto mīto, "meat only") written on it and a construction mallet. Stuck in the Jurassic Era, Mario and Princess Peach are attacked by a T-Rex. While escaping, they come across Yoshi's ancestor, who is busy meditating. They hop on his back, pleading him to eat the T-Rex. Confused, Genshi Yoshi turns around and screams upon seeing the dinosaur, which falls straight into his mouth and is swallowed whole. Surprised, Genshi Yoshi celebrates, having found the skill he was looking for through meditation: the ability to swallow a bigger prey. He invites the two to his village, only to find it deserted. His sister Yoppī appears, explaining that some days ago, a giant spiky turtle came and enslaved their kind to build him a palace. Using Mario's Mogura Bakudan, Bowser's palace is destroyed, and the two Yoshi siblings free their people. Bowser then sics an army of T-Rexes against them, but Genshi Yoshi effortlessly swallows them all, forcing Bowser to escape to another time period, chased by the heroes, who are rewarded by the Yoshis with a bunch of stone-made Dragon Coins. Glubbits are creatures that appear in Yoshi and the Mysterious Book. They are frog-like creatures with mouths shaped like bubble wands, who spit out bubbles that trap other creatures on contact. Glubbits who eat an apple will turn orange and produce bigger yellow bubbles which can trap up to three creatures inside it, while Glubbits who eat a heart turnip will become pink and produce heart-shaped bubbles that can trap up to two creatures. Glubbits that eat a hot pepper will turn red, gain spikes along the sides of their mouth, and spit out red bubbles that burst with enough force to scatter leaves and defeat Bunchabees and Big Bunchabees, as well as popping other bubbles nearby. When a Glubbit is covered in mud, its given type of bubble will become heavy and fall towards the ground. If a Yoshi eats a Glubbit, it will not only produce an egg, but also spit out a bubble. A Yoshi can have a Glubbit ride on its back, enabling it to belch out bubbles while Yoshi runs. Some Glubbits can be found buried underground while they sleep, requiring Yoshi to ground-pound the visible mound of dirt to force them out.

Gold Mini Slump Birds are gold Roc-like creatures in Donkey Kong Jungle Beat. They are larger, gold versions of Mini Slump Birds that appear only in Iguanagon's Realm. Unlike normal Mini Slump Birds, however, Gold Mini Slump Birds do not attack, but instead fly across the top of the screen over Donkey Kong and Hoofer. If the player manages to hit one with a Blood Pine, they are rewarded with fifty beats.
The Man-O-War is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III and Call of Duty: Mobile.

Grambi (called "Grams" by Queen Jaydes) is a character from Super Paper Mario, where he is introduced as the king of The Overthere. He is also Luvbi's father figure and although he appears grumpy at times, he still cares a lot for her. Just as Jaydes is based on Hades, the ancient Greek lord of the underworld, Grambi may be based on Zeus, the god of the sky and ruler of Mount Olympus in Greek mythology. Additionally, as The Overthere also borrows from Christian theism, certain aspects of Grambi are shared with the Christian God, such as his position as chief of the angelic Nimbis and his conflict with Bonechill (whose story greatly resembles that of Lucifer); however, Grambi is not credited with creating the world or life and is not omniscient or omnipotent. When Mario escorts Luvbi to The Overthere from The Underwhere, The Overthere is found under siege by Skellobits, with a majority of the Nimbis (the inhabitants of The Overthere) and Grambi being trapped in ice. Grambi was confronted by Bonechill when Mario and co. arrived at his shrine, and they have to defeat the villain. After the heroes defeat the villain, he recognizes them as the four prophesized heroes destined to find all the Pure Hearts and save the world, and it is then revealed that Luvbi was in fact the eighth and final Pure Heart, which was entrusted to Grambi and Jaydes, and she returns to her true form after a tearful goodbye with her parents.
