Hagure Teresa is a young Boo that appears in Super Mario Kart 1 of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. It is an adaptation of the Ghost item from Super Mario Kart. Tricked by the Kongs to take a fake shortcut in Ghost Valley, Mario and Lady end up in a dead end, where they find the Hagure Teresa all alone. Lady takes it with them, making it visibly happy. Later on, Mario and Donkey Kong Jr.'s karts are involved in a disastrous car crash. Everyone but Junior got out safe and sound from the situation, so Mario decides to take the ape to the hospital to tend to his injuries, abandoning the race. The Hagure Teresa follows Mario, and when faced against the Mole Biker Gang, who are instructed by Bowser to stop him (putting Junior's life at risk, despite their alliance), the Boo enters the kart's fuel pipe, turning it transparent and letting Mario avoid the incoming Monty Moles without any problem. After that, the Hagure Teresa is not seen again.

Haru () is the third sample talent in Mario Artist: Talent Studio. He has brown hair and wears bike goggles, a black and red shirt, camo safari pants, and red inline skates. According to his talent no namae profile, his hobby/specialty is cooking and his favorite food is chocolate. Haru also appears as a character in the sample movie "Hotcake". After his classmate Aiko calls him for a syrup recipe, he tells her about the sun honey, located in the south sea. He goes there at the same time as Aiko by skating on the water surface to show off his skating skills. Together with Aiko, he jumps into the sea to find a rabbit who gives him nuts that are later revealed to be the sun honey's seeds, which he then enjoys the sweetness of.
The MR6 is a semi-automatic pistol that appears in Call of Duty: Black Ops III and is a cut weapon in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4.

A Hane Mūcho is a secondary enemy that appears in Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story and its 3DS remake. They are blue Snifits with a pair of butterfly wings. Hane Mūcho are only seen aiding the Flifits that Bowser fights in Bumpsy Plains; Bowser can inhale several of their petals to leave them wilted. During a wilted Flifit's turn, the Hane Mūcho will appear to water them and restore them to normal, flying away right after. This role is somewhat similar to those of Beezos from Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars.

Kamek debuted in the Yoshi franchise as a main antagonist with Baby Bowser, his master. In his later appearances, he appeared as a boss and an antagonist in the core series and spin-offs; sometimes, he is playable in spin-offs.

The hopping nose bug is a non-sapient creature that makes minor appearances in the WarioWare games. It is a creature that resembles Wario's nose and hops around using its moustache like a cricket's legs.

Mass Weapon Lockout (initially Weapon Lockout prior to being upgraded) is a Martial cyber core in Call of Duty: Black Ops III. The default version locks down two enemies' weapons while upgraded version locks down four at a time. Enemies will attempt to unlock their weapons if not killed.

King Tetris is Bowser's persona and the main antagonist in the Super Mario Land 2 manga from the Super Mario series published by KC Deluxe and later returns in the third chapter of the next volume. It is the first "King persona" Bowser takes in the Super Mario Land miniseries. When first met, Bowser is simply wearing an Aztec mask with demonic traits, such as fangs and big pointy ears. He also dons pauldrons, but the rest of his body is not disguised, causing Mario to become suspicious upon seeing his spiked shell and tail. Also, in this first encounter, Bowser uses his magical "Tetris Powers" to move Tetriminos while wielding an Aztecan-looking magic staff. During the second part of the story (and in the next volume), he wears a less bulky mask with longer ears, now resembling horns, and more armor pieces adorned with spikes, covering most of his scaled body. While the tail is still visible, the shell is now covered under a cape with "KING TETRIS" written on it. He also mastered the use of the Tetris Power without the need of using the staff. King Tetris seems to have been an actual person in the Tetris tribe, famous for having hidden a great treasure that can only be reached by the greatest Tetris player. He then disappeared for ages, leaving the Tetris throne empty. Lemmy Koopa (known as Hip Koopa in the DIC cartoons) is one of the Koopalings, a clan of seven siblings who act as leaders of Bowser's Minions under Bowser (originally considered his children). Lemmy is the smallest of the group and is often associated with childish traits due to his stature and ditzy personality. He is identified by his multicolored mohawk (and later a yellow pony-tail), crossed eyes, and the magical ball he balances atop in most appearances; his special abilities also involve bouncy balls.

The M. Red P-Goomba (presumably short for "Mad Red Paragoomba") is an enemy in the game Super Princess Peach. When it sees Princess Peach, it charges at her. If it falls off a ledge, it can fly back up to the surface. They are mostly encountered in Fury Volcano.

The MX Garand (known as the M2 Raider in pre-release) is a semi-automatic Assault Rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III. Only available in multiplayer, it is a Black Market-exclusive weapon that was added to the game on February 8th, 2016.

The Mad G. P-Troopa (presumably short for "Mad Green Paratroopa") is an enemy in Super Princess Peach. These Paratroopas live on Vibe Island and appear in most of the worlds on the island. Like all Paratroopas, they have wings, and they also have green shells, are red in the face, and puff smoke out of their ears. They fly above the ground and charge at Princess Peach if she comes near.

The Mekakuppa is a giant robotic Bowser, appearing on two occasions in the Super Mario World story arc in Super Mario-kun. In chapter 2 of volume 2, Bowser is angry at the failures of his minions, so he activates the Mekakuppa, knowing Mario and his friends are headed to Vanilla Dome. The trio is attacked by the robot, which tries to stomp with its feet, then crushes them with metal nasal mucus. Mario tries to fight back using Yoshi as a bat, but ends up angering the Mekakuppa, which pulls out a giant drill from its wrist. While trying to hit Mario, the Mekakuppa creates a hole in the Vanilla Dome, creating a connection with Vanilla Dome 3's lake. From that, the Dolphins fall into the lake and take Mario, Luigi, and Yoshi to the surface, where Mario plugs the hole, trapping the robot. However, the Mekakuppa resurfaces and knocks out the trio. Mario flies away with a Power Balloon and finds a 3-Up Moon in the sky and becomes Moon Mario. While being unfazed by the robot's laser, Mario grabs a Cape Feather in the Item Stock, then tickles the Mekakuppa's nose, making him sneeze out all of his mechanical components. Mario then rebuilds the robot into a Ferris wheel. In the first part of chapter 11 of volume 4, while traversing the Bowser's Castle hall full of Bowser Statues, a giant Bowser Statue emerges from the lava. The Microphone is a character in Donkey Kong 64. He is a sentient microphone with blue eyes, a mustache, and a boxing referee's tuxedo. In the final boss fight against K. Rool - a boxing match between him and all five playable Kongs - the Microphone serves as the ring announcer in between rounds, giving very dramatic descriptions for each Kong. He moves around by hopping.
The Malice is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III and Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare.
Minikyura are bat enemies in Super Mario Land 2 - 6 Golden Coins.

Mogura Mario is a transformation that Mario comes across in Super Mario-kun volume 1. Upon reaching a wall that blocks Mario from proceeding in the level on ground and in the air, Isshī gives him another of the hypothetical Super Mario Bros. 5s power-ups, which transforms him into Mogura Mario to let him proceed underground (due to the absence of Warp Pipes). In this form, Mario wears a Monty Mole costume and can dig through the ground.

Mr. Sparkles is a character that first appears in WarioWare Gold. He is a bodybuilder who regularly weightlifts his signature frying pans, and is notable for, besides his build, his enthusiasm and constant smiling. Mr. Sparkles (accompanied by two Alien Bunnies) first appears on a television program which catches 5-Volt's attention. He advertises a set of frying pans, but advises customers not to buy them until they get into shape, as the pans are allegedly heavy. Out of boredom, 5-Volt decides to partake in the bodybuilding exercise herself, helping her retrieve 9-Volt's dropped Nintendo 3DS later on. Mr. Sparkles appears as a deception in the Sneaky Gamer mode of the game, lifting 9-Volt's television rack in place of 5-Volt to reveal himself, and may also appear on TV when it is on. In WarioWare: Move It!, Mr. Sparkles, now dressed in a toga, appears as the host of Megagame Muscles, singing the song that plays during the mode.

The Mangler Helmet is an item in the Call of Duty: Black Ops III Zombies map, Gorod Krovi. It can be found on a mannequin in the Department Store's second floor, in a corner directly to the left of the L-CAR 9 Wall Buy and across from the barrier. It returns in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 as a Cursed Relic that, when activated, disables the Arsenal utility,

Mototin 2-gō is a living with limbs and a fountain pen on his head, just like the character he is named after, Mototin, acting as his second avatar. He appears in some Mario Paint chapters of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. According to Daisy's lies in Super Mario Land 2 - 6-tsu no Kinka 3, Princess Peach became the ruler of the Toads thanks to Mototin 2-gō. The Toads, oppressed by Bowser, fished Mototin 2-gō out of the river and he was ready to grant them a wish by drawing the subject on his Mario Paint copy and materializing it. The starving Toads drew a peach, and a giant peach appeared, and from inside it, Peach and her animal pals emerged and saved the Toads from Bowser. In Super Donkey Kong with Mario 1, he replaces Mototin in the cover and final page of the Mario Paint chapter, boasting about his loyal fans.

Mr. Arcade is a character who appears in American commercials made by Coleco for tabletop versions of arcade games such as the Donkey Kong tabletop arcade game and the Table Top Donkey Kong Jr. Game & Watch. He has shrinking powers. In the first commercial, Donkey Kong (played by an actor in a gorilla suit) is hogging a Donkey Kong arcade game and frightening the other patrons. They call out for Mr. Arcade, who comes and shrinks the machine. He lures Donkey Kong away by taking the tabletop version with him. He tells Donkey Kong that its portability means he can take it home with him. The commercial ends with Donkey Kong playing the game on a treetop. In the second commercial, Mr. Arcade meets a group of people watching Donkey Kong Jr. (portrayed by a real-life chimpanzee) play the Donkey Kong Jr. arcade game. Since Donkey Kong Jr. is not skilled at the game, Mr. Arcade helps him by shrinking the arcade machine into a portable handheld game so he can save Donkey Kong at home, resulting in Donkey Kong Jr. giving him a kiss. The narration at the end of the commercial then says that Mr. Arcade also "shrinks prices" of Coleco's tabletop arcade games.

Ninja Heihōmaru is a Shy Guy ninja who appears in Super Mario: Yoshi Island 2 of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. He is a Shy-Guy wearing a typical ninja outfit, and his mask can change expression. He carries a katana, but does not use it, and can also apply a propeller to become a Fly Guy. After the events of the game, Baby Bowser grows tired of Kamek's failing magic, and hires Ninja Heihōmaru to use his ninjitsu techniques to achieve his revenge on Yoshi's Island. Using his Froggy companion, Ninja Heihōmaru adds a fake Yoshi's snout to him, enlarges it, and then fuse with him, becoming his uvula. First, he and Baby Bowser pass Froggy for the Yoshi God, trapping most of the Yoshis during their festival, then they ambush Green Yoshi and Baby Mario and make Froggy swallow them. Soon enough, Baby Bowser gives the same treatment to four disrespectful Spear Guys. Inside Froggy's stomach, Ninja Heihōmaru, appearing in the frog's uvula, informs the prisoner of their impending doom via the stomach acid, then prevents their escape by turning in a Dangling Ghost and pushing back down the throat. To escape, Baby Mario instructs the Spear Guys to aim at the uvula. The pain makes Froggy explode, releasing Ninja Heihōmaru and the swallowed victim. Without Froggy, Ninja Heihōmaru turns into a Fly Guy and escapes with Baby Bowser, but Baby Mario reaches them with the help of a Nep-Enut and lands, soiled diaper-first, on Baby Bowser's head, causing him and Ninja Heihōmaru to fall into the sea
The Magic Wheel is a utility in Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It gives the player a random weapon much like the Mystery Box or 3D Printer.

Omni Nom is a minor character that appears in WarioWare: Move It! It has the appearance of a round, blue alien with a detached mouth, small wings, bird legs and an antenna with a star on it. It also appears to be flying with its own fish-based version of the Oinker. Omni Nom appears in the "Sweet Dreams, Sweeter Fruit" stage in a flashback as Orbulon regains his memory, where it is seen flying alongside Orbulon and his Oinker.

Oumu is the second to last Debeso to be born, who appears in chapters 3 and 4 of Super Mario World! Yoshi no Tamago of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. He hides his true nature by covering his outward belly button with a cross band-aid. Born one thousand years before the events of the manga, he was the previous Devil Yoshi before shedding into a Debeso. One millennium later, discovering that Bowser intends to use his soon-to-be born brother, he appears to Mario and his friends to aid them in their journey to stop the Koopa King and save Mother Yoshi. At first, the group finds him annoying, especially when he gives a kiss on the cheek to Peach and seemingly directs them to the wrong island. When the heroes are kidnapped by the Pirate Koopalings, Wendy claims that she will not throw them to the sharks, if Mario reciprocates her feelings. Mario refuses, so Oumu knocks him out with a mallet he summoned with a magic wand, and maneuvers him like a puppet to satisfy Wendy. When the pirate ship crashes onto a rock, Oumu bonks his head onto a mast and gets knocked out for the rest of the chapter, while Mario regains consciousness and the Koopalings all fall overboard. In the last chapter, Oumu first save the heroes from drowning by summoning with his wand his eggshell after Bowser destroys the Pirate Ship they stole, then suggest into piling the enemies onto the eggshell to create a ladder to the top of the Devil Yoshi no Tō. Peekabruiser is the first boss of Donkey Kong Bananza. It is a cube-shaped octopus-like creature formed out of multiple Peekaboopoids that is fought in the Lagoon Layer. It is created by Grumpy Kong after Void Company confronts Donkey Kong and Pauline for the first time. It attacks by firing Peekaboopoids from its mouth, and moves quickly around the arena to avoid being hit. It changes its body into concrete in order to defend itself from normal attacks, but this can be bypassed by using the Kong Bananza. When enough damage is taken, it breaks apart and turns into a mass of Peekaboopoids, running away and forming a hill while Peekaboopoids attack Donkey Kong. In this state, its weak point is exposed and can be attacked to damage and defeat the boss. It reappears in the Landfill Layer under the name Re-Peekabruiser when Grumpy Kong again constructs it in an attempt to prevent Donkey Kong from progressing further. During this fight, it moves faster and when it begins to form a hill, it now creates a pit around it to trap Donkey Kong. It is one of the three bosses in the game that cannot be rematched after its last defeat; the others being Mad Mixer and Poppy Kong. In the DK Island & Emerald Rush DLC, a statue of Peekabruiser can be collected and placed in the East Ruins nearby DK's Tree House on DK Island.

The Master Key is a Gun Perk featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. The Campaign version of the Erad submachine gun is equipped with a Master Key by default. In Multiplayer and Zombies, the Master Key is only available to the Epic Cerberus variant of the Erad.

Plok is the protagonist of and its webcomic sequel. He is a large-eyed creature with the special ability to throw his arms and legs away, an easy-to-anger personality, and a tendency to explode when aggravated, who rules as the king of Akrillic Island, asserting his authority by placing flags with his face on them throughout the island, and is the nemesis of the Flea Queen. Plok appears twice in the Super Mario franchise, once on the planet Hösndösn in the German Club Nintendo comic "Super Mario: Verloren in der Zeit", taking part in the "intergalactical Olympics" of Hösndösn. He seems to be very sportive as he and Mario are the last two competitors in the games; it is also mentioned that they are breaking several records. Plok also appears as a sticker in the eponymous Mario Paint Players' Guide animation tutorial. Both of these appearances also feature an enemy from the game, the Flea.

A Propeller Piranha, originally known as a Hootie the Blue Fish (pluralized Hooties), is a purple species of Piranha Plant that appears in Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island and Yoshi's New Island. Propeller Piranhas bear a strong resemblance to Jumping Piranha Plants and Piranha Pests; they attack in a manner similar to the latter, but unlike other Piranha Plants in the games, the Propeller Piranhas are near-invincible enemies for a Yoshi.

Rainbi is a Nimbi residing in The Overthere in Super Paper Mario. Her name is derived from "rain" and "Nimbi". Initially she is frozen in ice in the shrine of Sector 4. Bowser can free her from the ice with the Fire Breath, after which she thanks the heroes for saving her and asks them to do "what thou canst for the others". Later in the game, she is not found in the shrine. According to Tippi's tattle, she believes in fate and desires to meet the fortune-teller Merluvlee.

The Magnetic Bolt Carrier is a weapon attachment featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is only available for the FHR-40 submachine gun, to which it is an integral attachment. It allows the FHR-40 to offset modest range with an extreme fire rate.

Samus Aran, commonly known as simply Samus, is an occasional crossover character in the Super Mario franchise and the main protagonist of the series. She is an intergalactic bounty hunter that was orphaned at a young age and raised by the avian race. They infused her with their own DNA so that she would tolerate their harsh planet, and trained her in combat so that she could use the . After venturing out as a young woman, Samus briefly served as a member of the , after which she decided to become a contracted bounty hunter. The first Metroid game was developed by Nintendo R&D1, the studio that had developed Super Mario Land and the Wario Land series. Samus was designed by Wario's creator Hiroji Kiyotake. Comics involving Wario have occasionally made explicit references to Samus, potentially alluding to their shared studio history.

Screech is an enemy character in Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest and Donkey Kong Land 2. He is a dark-brown parrot with red tail feathers, a white beak, big yellow eyes with two small pupils, and three claws on each talon. Screech has an identical role between both games, where he appears at the second half of his own level, Screech's Sprint, where the Kongs must enter an Animal Barrel to transform into Squawks to race Screech, both of which compete to cross the finish line first. The race ends when either Screech or Squawks crosses the line first. If Screech wins, the Kongs lose a life. In the ending's Cast of Characters, Screech is categorized under Lazy Landlubbers. Screech appears in two pieces of promotional artwork, including the game cover, where he fights Squawks using a baseball bat, and in a bramble area, where Diddy and Dixie are seen passing by him. Screech has his own theme music, "Bad Bird Rag," which plays during his race. In the remake of Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest, Screech's theme music plays while Diddy Kong and Dixie Kong (transformed into Rambi) are being chased by King Zing through the last stretch of the level Rambi Rumble. In Donkey Konga 3, Screech makes a cameo appearance in Freestyle Zone, as one of the enemies whose artwork appears on screen as the player hits the DK Bongos.

Sue is a character from the Super Mario Land manga adaptation in the Super Mario series from KC Deluxe. At first glance, she is a petite cave girl with pink hair in a side ponytail, big eyes and a small pair of upper fangs, and wears an animal-print two-piece and a flower on her head. In reality, she is a transformed Suu, but when she reverts to her original spider-like form, she still retains the human head and her limbs are more human-like. She appears in chapters 3 and 4 of Super Mario Land, but also appears in the "find the differences" page and later in the 4koma page to give the solution of the game. After watching how miserably the moai of Easton Kingdom have failed to stop Mario and Mecha Kuribō, Tatanga orders the Kumos and Suu to take their place, much to boss Hiyoihoi's frustration. After easily escaping (once more) from the Batadon and Tokotoko, Mario and Mecha Kuribō encounter Sue, who offers to guide them through a "secure" cave. Mecha Kuribō (who is actually Princess Peach in disguise) does not trust her, but Mario quickly falls for her beauty and follows her. Mecha Kuribō gives her the benefit of the doubt, but yells at her when she gets lunged by a swarm of Suu. Mario protects her and quickly gets rid of the spiders (disappointing Sue). The girl then points to a Hidden Block with a Lift Block inside that Mario takes, entering a bonus area. Now alone, Sue drops a portrait of pop-idol "by accident". The Mandate is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty Online. It can be switched between assault rifle and shotgun mode.

The Suppon no Karon is a species of Dry Bones in Super Mario-kun that, in the future, evolved to have shapeshifting bones. Only one of them, the Kāmenētā, appears only in volume 5. In the future, Bowser has lost his title of king, so he hires a famous Suppon no Karon, the Kāmenētā, to go back to the past and kill Mario, before he defeats him in Super Mario World (the moment he considers the beginning of his downfall). The only item capable of destroying a Suppon no Karon is the Super Kōra, which Princess Peach from the future sends to Mario during his fight with the Kāmenētā.

Taj is a blue elephant and a genie who lives on Timber's Island. Taj appears mainly in Diddy Kong Racing and its Nintendo DS remake, though he has also appeared in Super Mario publications exclusively published in Japan. Taj could have possibly been inspired from the real-world , considering his basis from Indian culture.

Tanooki is a character briefly appearing in the Super Mario Bros. comic "Tanooki Suits Me." His name is a reference to the Tanooki Suit, and was the very first tailor to set up shop in the Mushroom Kingdom, whose specialty was to create Tanooki Suits. Tanooki is first mentioned by an elderly man who notices Mario in a Tanooki Suit, commenting that it has been years that he has seen such a fine example of Tanooki-tailoring. He goes on to explain that Tanooki was the first tailor of the Mushroom Kingdom and the creator of the Tanooki Suit, whose trademark was to sew a tail on the back of every suit he made. The suits became very popular, with everyone wanting a Tanooki Suit, as each had special powers, such as cleaning one's house and turning one into a statue. However, Tanooki grew tired of trying to keep up with the demand for Tanooki Suits, and, one day, closed his shop and disappeared. The man tells Mario to take care of his Tanooki Suit, as a genuine one is rare nowadays.
The MX9 (stylized MX-9) is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 and Call of Duty: Mobile.

The Three Shadows, originally known as the Shadow Sirens, are three shadowy witches in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door and its Nintendo Switch remake who serve the Shadow Queen. They consist of Beldam, Marilyn, and Vivian, who is later replaced by Doopliss once Vivian splinters from the group and becomes one of Mario's party members. The Three Shadows aid Grodus and the X-Nauts in their quest for the Crystal Stars, and attempt to retrieve the Magical Map from Mario and his party to free their queen, though their help to Grodus and the X-Nauts is only out of convenience of using their resources rather than a true loyalty. They manipulate Grodus into believing he will control the queen upon her release; however, once the queen is free, they betray Grodus to serve the queen directly. Beldam, the leader of the Three Shadows, is often forgetful and on more than one occasion blames Vivian for her own faults. Despite this, Beldam appears to have the strongest affinity for magic among the group. Marilyn is the biggest and physically strongest of the sisters, though she appears to lack communication skills and generally only grunts "Guh". Unlike Marilyn, who is happy to follow Beldam's every command, Vivian is more independently minded. The youngest of the sisters, she eventually defects from the group due to their mistreatment of her and instead joins Mario to help him stop the queen's revival. The Thunderbirdo is a purple, colossal Birdo who only appears in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Toad Warriors". King-of-the-Road Koopa, attacking the Rebel Fort in Car Land, gives Mouser orders to call for the Thunderbirdo, a member of the Koopa Pack who is Koopa's ultimate weapon whom he brings forward on a car, to use in the attack. Once in position, the Thunderbirdo fires a giant egg at the Rebel Fort, which explodes violently upon the building, heavily damaging it. After this first attack on the Rebel Fort, the Thunderbirdo continues blasting the building with more explosive eggs. Later, after Mario and Princess Toadstool drive away from the semi-demolished Rebel Fort in a spaghetti sauce tanker truck, the Thunderbirdo, riding a car driven by Mouser, tries attacking them. Before the Thunderbirdo fires an egg at the tanker truck, Princess Toadstool, who is riding on the truck's top, throws a Bob-Omb bag into the Thunderbirdo's snout. The Thunderbirdo unwittingly swallows it on reflex, causing it to blow up. When the Thunderbirdo is introduced, its lower body is depicted as green with a yellow belly rather than purple with a white belly; later, just before its explosion, the shot of a panicked Mouser also shows its tail as green.

Ura Yoshi is Yoshi's counterpart from the flipside world, appearing in volume 2 of Super Mario-kun. He is the exact mirror image of Yoshi: violent, asocial, and with scars and tattoos of Dinosaur Land on his body. Mario wakes up in the flipside world, but then stomps Ura Yoshi's tail, making him angry. After he tries to eat him, Ura Yoshi realizes that Mario is not a Mask Koopa, his enemies. Mario decides to help him, but when he tries to make a combined attack (like he does with his Yoshi), Ura Yoshi punches him back, not intending to work together with him. After that, Mario defeats the Mask Koopa army and wakes up in the normal world, happy to have the always friendly Yoshi back.
The Maddox RFB is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile, and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

Wave the Swallow, commonly known as simply Wave, is a character from the franchise and the mechanic of the Babylon Rogues. She first appears in Sonic Riders. In the Super Mario franchise, Wave appears in a few of the games in the Mario & Sonic series.

Winbi is a Nimbi residing in The Overthere in Super Paper Mario. Her name is derived from winter, just like many other Nimbis that have month and season derived names. She can be found in the shrine of Sector 4. She is initially frozen and Bowser can free her from the ice with the Fire Breath. Still a bit shaken up, she thanks Bowser for rescuing him. She loves movies and is a frequent visitor of video stores.
